channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Seeks International Search for Online Casino Owners Who Lost 100 Billion Tenge
item.description: The alleged organizers of an illegal online casino, which defrauded Kazakh citizens of 100 billion tenge, have been placed on an international wanted list. Investigations revealed that Ukrainian citizens, with the help of local IT specialists and financiers, facilitated the transfer of funds abroad.

item.title: Afghan Women Battle Breast Cancer Amid Poverty and Limited Healthcare Access
item.description: Afghan women diagnosed with breast cancer face significant challenges, including poverty, limited access to specialized healthcare, and difficulties covering treatment costs. Border closures and visa issues further complicate travel for treatment, while delayed diagnosis and inadequate facilities exacerbate the struggle.

item.title: New Entrepreneurship Support System Launched in Jizzakh Region, Uzbekistan
item.description: A new entrepreneurship support system has been established in Uzbekistan's Jizzakh region, featuring a showroom for production equipment. This initiative aims to become a new mechanism for supporting businesses in other regions, contributing to poverty reduction and income growth by fostering citizen initiatives and providing necessary resources.

item.title: Kazakhstan Police Receive Over 4 Million Emergency Calls Since Start of Year
item.description: Kazakhstan's emergency police number, 102, has received over 4.1 million calls since the beginning of the year, averaging 12,000-15,000 daily, or one call every 6-7 seconds. The police also utilize other channels like a mobile app and an 'SOS' button for reporting incidents.

item.title: United Airlines considers launching flights to Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan
item.description: United Airlines is exploring the possibility of launching flights to Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, but flight restrictions over Russia pose a challenge. The airline's CEO mentioned interest in Central Asian markets, with a network planning executive visiting both countries to assess prospects. Direct flights are currently not feasible due to airspace limitations, but future possibilities are being considered.

item.title: Analysis: Is the Pakistan-Taliban confrontation real or a staged political game?
item.description: The confrontation between Pakistan and the Taliban raises questions about Islamabad's strategic objectives and the future of their relations. This analysis explores whether the conflict is a genuine clash of interests, a managed confrontation to contain opponents, or a continuation of Pakistan's historical security strategy. The article examines the gap between Pakistan's expectations and the Taliban's conduct, noting the complex history of cooperation and dependency.

item.title: Iran Designates UK Intelligence Service MI6 as Terrorist Organization
item.description: Iran has declared the UK's MI6 intelligence service a hostile organization and listed its Navy and Air Force as terrorist groups. This action follows London's inclusion of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps in its counter-terrorism legislation.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Central Bank Lowers Key Interest Rate to 15.75%
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank has reduced its key interest rate to 15.75%, signaling a gradual easing of monetary conditions. The impact on mortgage costs depends on how quickly and significantly this reduction is reflected in lending rates, according to analysts.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Foil and Sabre Fencers Secure Gold at Asian Championships (U23)
item.description: Kazakhstan's young fencers have claimed two gold medals at the U23 Asian Championships. The men's épée team defeated Hong Kong in a close final, while the women's sabre team also secured victory. These wins add to the nation's growing reputation in the sport.

item.title: Kremlin: Putin Will Respond if Zelensky Calls
item.description: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov stated that Russian President Vladimir Putin would respond if Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky calls. Ushakov noted that Ukraine has been signaling readiness for dialogue through various channels. He suggested that initial negotiations on resolving the conflict should be in a trilateral format involving Russia, the US, and Ukraine.

item.title: Iran Declares UK Navy and Air Force 'Terrorist Organizations'
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry has declared the British Navy and Air Force as 'terrorist organizations'. The ministry also placed the UK's Secret Intelligence Service (MI6) on its list of 'hostile groups'. This decision, based on a Supreme National Security Council resolution, is in response to recent UK actions against Iran, including its alleged involvement in conflicts and designation of the IRGC as terrorist.

item.title: Kazakhstan's FlyArystan Low-Cost Airline to Add New Airbus A320neo Aircraft
item.description: Kazakhstan's low-cost carrier FlyArystan will receive a new Airbus A320neo aircraft, seating 188 passengers, from Airbus in Toulouse in the first half of November. The aircraft, named Atria, will enhance the airline's fleet, increasing the proportion of new-generation aircraft to about half. This addition supports job creation in aviation and related sectors.

item.title: UN Highlights Evolving Humanitarian Needs in Afghanistan Amidst Returns and Shocks
item.description: The UN Special Trust Fund for Afghanistan notes evolving humanitarian needs due to migrant returns, climate shocks, and economic pressures. Future programs will prioritize local communities and expand successful initiatives. Afghanistan faces a major humanitarian crisis, with millions requiring assistance due to food insecurity, poverty, and resource shortages.

item.title: Tribal Elder Shot Dead in His Home in Daikundi Province
item.description: Local sources reported that Haji Ghulam Mohammad, a prominent tribal elder, was shot dead in his room in Ghochan village, Shahristan district, Daikundi province. This incident follows another mysterious killing of a young man in the Kian area of Khadir district a week prior, raising public concerns.

item.title: Taliban and Pakistani Forces Clash Again at Torkham Border Crossing
item.description: Local sources report renewed clashes between Taliban fighters and Pakistani forces at the Torkham border crossing. The fighting, which began around noon, caused humanitarian organizations to evacuate staff and led the Taliban to remove deportees from a nearby camp. Clashes erupted after the Taliban attempted to set up a checkpoint.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Retain Pensioner Teachers, Ministry of Education States
item.description: The Ministry of Education in Kyrgyzstan has announced that teachers who are already retired will not be dismissed. Approximately 15,000 teachers of retirement age currently work in schools. The ministry aims to avoid age-based discrimination and is exploring new professional roles for older educators, such as mentoring and consulting.

item.title: US Plans to Deport Afghans to Their Homeland Via Pakistan, Drawing Criticism
item.description: The Trump administration reportedly plans to deport Afghan migrants detained in the U.S. to Afghanistan via Pakistan, with flights potentially starting soon. Advocacy groups and Democratic lawmakers have condemned the plan, citing broken promises to Afghan allies who aided U.S. forces and warning of dangerous consequences upon return to Taliban-ruled Afghanistan.

item.title: Astana to Restrict Traffic on Select Streets from November 5-7
item.description: Astana will implement temporary traffic restrictions on certain streets from November 5 to 7 due to preparations for international political events. The measures will involve special state, law enforcement, and armed forces resources. Military aviation training flights will also occur in the capital's airspace starting November 1.

item.title: Kazakhstan Imposes New Entry Requirements for Foreign Nationals
item.description: Kazakhstan has implemented new regulations for foreign citizens entering and temporarily staying in the country. Citizens from certain visa-free countries will need an electronic permit before traveling to Kazakhstan. This requirement will be phased in and become mandatory by July 1, 2027.

item.title: Taliban Demolish Homes in Sar-e Pol, Residents Accuse of Ethnic Cleansing
item.description: Taliban forces reportedly demolished approximately 20 homes in Sayedabad Arabia village, Sar-e Pol Province, and transferred the land to Pashtun Kuchi nomads. Residents, claiming Arab descent, accuse the Taliban governor of ethnic discrimination and ethnic cleansing, citing the displacement of indigenous people and insults directed at residents during the demolition.

item.title: Suspect Arrested in Shymkent for Alleged 4 Billion Tenge Fraud Against Housing Investors
item.description: Police in Kazakhstan have arrested a 45-year-old man in Shymkent, who was internationally wanted for allegedly defrauding housing investors. The suspect, along with accomplices, is accused of collecting funds for an apartment complex in Astana without proper permits. Over 292 investors reportedly lost more than 4 billion tenge.

item.title: Almaty Resident Arrested for Calling for Mass Truck Blockade
item.description: An Almaty resident has been detained for 15 days for inciting a mass blockade of trucks in the city. The city's police department identified the individual behind a video appeal urging drivers to protest weight restrictions. He was charged with organizing an unauthorized mass event.

item.title: Turkey Nominates Former Envoy Feridun Sinirlioglu for UN Secretary-General Position
item.description: Turkey has nominated Feridun Sinirlioglu, its former foreign minister and current OSCE secretary-general, for the position of United Nations secretary-general. The nomination letter was submitted to the UN General Assembly and Security Council presidents. Sinirlioglu previously served as Turkey's permanent representative to the UN from 2016 to 2023.

item.title: Kazakhstan's November: Elections, Mortgage Programs, and New Air Routes
item.description: November in Kazakhstan brings significant events including maslikhat elections and the second stage of the 'Umai' women's mortgage program. The country will also introduce QazETA, open new road sections in Astana, and launch direct flights between Almaty and Tokyo. Astronomical phenomena and premieres are also expected.

item.title: UN: Health Services in Afghanistan Reduced or Closed Due to Funding Shortage
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reports that a lack of funding has forced health centers in Afghanistan to reduce services or close. This comes as one-third of nutrition centers have shut down, and over four million children under six will need treatment for acute malnutrition next year. OCHA has requested $1.7 billion for 17.5 million vulnerable people, with only 33% secured.

item.title: Binance Compensates Users for 90% of Funds Lost in Major Hacking Incident
item.description: The cryptocurrency exchange Binance has announced it has returned 90% of funds lost by users in a recent hacking attack. The company has allocated $6.3 billion to cover losses for BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC tokens. The remaining 10% for less liquid tokens will take longer to compensate.

item.title: Belarus Appoints Non-Resident Ambassador to Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced that Alexander Sirigovich Ugorodnik has been appointed as Belarus's new non-resident ambassador to Afghanistan. The ambassador presented his credentials to the acting Taliban Foreign Minister, Amir Khan Muttaqi, expressing a commitment to developing trade and economic relations between the two countries.

item.title: Armenia Overhauls Residency Permit Rules, Introducing New Investment Path
item.description: Armenia has implemented significant reforms to its "Law on Foreigners," altering permanent residency rules. The business route now requires three years of temporary residency first. A new direct path to a five-year permanent residency is available for significant economic investors, bypassing the standard business route.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Urges Global Attention to Mountain Ecosystem Protection
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is calling on the international community to focus more on protecting mountain ecosystems and increase funding for mountain nations. At the COP17 conference in Yerevan, Kyrgyzstan proposed establishing a special mountain program within the Global Environment Facility and a global center for mountain region sustainability in Bishkek.

item.title: Astana to Restrict Traffic and Conduct Military Aviation Flights November 5-7
item.description: Astana will temporarily restrict traffic on certain streets from November 5 to 7, 2026, due to preparations for international political events. Special state and law enforcement agencies, along with the Armed Forces of Kazakhstan, will ensure security. Military aviation training flights will also occur.

item.title: Kazakhstan and OPEC+ Agree to Maintain December Oil Production Quotas
item.description: Key OPEC+ participants, including Kazakhstan, have preliminarily agreed to keep December oil production targets unchanged. This decision aligns with expectations of further policy adjustments being postponed until next year. The group is assessing member countries' production capacities to determine 2027 baseline levels.

item.title: Reservoir Explosion at Rogun Dam Construction Site in Tajikistan
item.description: An explosion occurred at a reservoir during the construction of the Rogun Dam in Tajikistan. Authorities claim no one was injured, while independent media report casualties. The State Supervision Service for Industrial and Mining Safety attributed the incident to a rupture in a technical water collection reservoir, which flooded workers in a tunnel. First aid was provided, and workers returned to their jobs.

item.title: Kazakhstan's processed agricultural exports increase, exceeding 54% of total
item.description: Kazakhstan's exports of value-added agricultural products are steadily growing. In the first eight months of 2026, processed agricultural exports reached $3.04 billion, a 35.1% increase year-on-year. Processed goods now account for 54.1% of total agricultural exports, indicating improved competitiveness.

item.title: Polish Prime Minister Refuses Compromise with President Amid Constitutional Dispute
item.description: Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk has rejected any compromise with President Andrzej Duda regarding the constitutional tribunal dispute. The President returned to Warsaw from Senegal and met with the tribunal's dismissed speaker, while Tusk criticized the move, vowing to uphold the rule of law.

item.title: New Nationwide Polio Vaccination Campaign to Begin Tomorrow in Afghanistan
item.description: A new polio vaccination campaign is set to launch across Afghanistan tomorrow. The initiative aims to combat the spread of polio within the country. Health officials are urging widespread participation to ensure the campaign's success.

item.title: Polish PM Tusk Accuses Russia of Supporting Opponents Amidst Political Crisis
item.description: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk accused Russia of fueling the current political crisis in Poland, stating that an "army of Russian bots" on the internet supports his opponents. Tusk criticized the Law and Justice party, President Andrzej Duda, and current President Karol Nawrocki for undermining the rule of law. He highlighted attempts to resolve issues with the Constitutional Tribunal being obstructed.

item.title: Kazakhstan Begins Phased Introduction of Electronic Entry Permit System
item.description: Kazakhstan commenced a phased rollout of the QazETA electronic entry permit system on November 1. Initially, it applies to citizens of visa-free countries and EAEU nations at Aktau airport and select land border crossings. The permit will become mandatory by July 1, 2027.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan Companies Sign Agreements Worth $95 Million
item.description: Companies from Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan have signed agreements and contracts totaling $95 million following a trade and economic mission in Bishkek. The agreements were reached during the Second Forum of Interregional Cooperation between the two countries. Discussions focused on export expansion and joint investment projects.

item.title: Criminal Case Launched Against Imarat Development Management in Tashkent
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated against the management of Imarat Development LLC in Tashkent. The company, based in Sergeli district, allegedly failed to inform buyers that homes were being built in the Tashkent region and did not return funds.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Corn Fields Exceed Astana's Area After 60% Growth
item.description: Corn cultivation in Kazakhstan has surged by 60% to 106,000 hectares, surpassing the area of Astana. This expansion is driven by the demand from new processing plants, including 'KazKrakhmal' in the Turkestan region, which processes 150,000 tons of corn annually. The Ministry of Agriculture reported this growth.
